title: In situ Compressive Loading and Correlative Noninvasive Imaging of the Bone-periodontal Ligament-tooth Fibrous Joint
protocol: House animals under pathogen-free conditions in accordance with the guidelines of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) and the National Institute of Health (NIH).
Provide animals with standard hard-pellet rat chow and water ad libitum.
Euthanize animals via carbon dioxide asphyxiation followed by bilateral thoracotomy.
Remove rat mandibles by gently severing membranous tissue and muscle tissue attachments while preserving the entire mandible, including the coronoid process and the condylar process.
Separate hemimandibles by carefully cutting the fibrous tissue of mandibular symphysis with a scalpel blade.
Prepare specimens for in situ compressive loading by immobilizing them on a steel stub using a material significantly stiffer than the experimental specimen.
Align the occlusal surface of the molar(s) parallel with the AFM metal specimen disc using a straight edge in both planes (mesial-distal and buccal-lingual).
Create a trough surrounding the molars to contain excess liquid and maintain tissue hydration during loading.
Etch the surface of the tooth of interest with 35% phosphoric acid gel for 15 seconds on the occlusal surface.
Rinse the etched surface thoroughly with deionized water and dry it using an air/water syringe or a compressed-air canister.
Spread a drop of bonding agent into open cusps in a thin layer with an explorer.
Cure the composite with a dental curing light to set the bonding agent.
Remove excess bonding agent from adjacent teeth with a fine scalpel or razor blade.
Place flowable dental composite on the surface following preparation and spread it into grooves of the molar(s) of interest using a dental explorer.
Expose the composite to dental curing light for 30 seconds.
Mold an occlusal buildup of about 3-4 mm using a dental resin composite from the occlusal plane of the molar(s) and cure with dental curing light for 30 seconds.
Reduce the top of the composite buildup to a flat surface parallel to the occlusal plane using a straight edge and high-speed hand piece.
Secure the specimen with the composite buildup on the anvil of the loading stage.
Place an articulating paper on the surface of the composite.
Load the specimen to a finite load to check for concentric or eccentric loading.
Place TBS-soaked Kimwipe around the specimen to ensure hydration.
Make a trough around the specimen and fill it with TBS to keep the organ hydrated during imaging.
Input peak load and displacement rate into the Deben software to compress the molar to a desired peak load at a specified displacement rate following immobilization of the hemimandible.
Backfill PTA staining solution into a clean 1.8 ml glass carpule and place loaded carpule into syringe.
Inject solution slowly (5 min/carpule) into the PDL-space of adjacent teeth.
Repeat injection steps until about 5 full carpules (9 ml) of solution are injected.
Soak prepped specimens overnight in remaining PTA solution (8 hr).
